# mcrl annotation

[Command reference](README.md)

Manage graph annotations.

```text
Aliases:
  annotation, annotations
```

| Subcommand | Description |
|---|---|
| [`annotation create`](#mcrl-annotation-create) | Create a graph annotation |
| [`annotation delete`](#mcrl-annotation-delete) | Delete a graph annotation |
| [`annotation list`](#mcrl-annotation-list) | List graph annotations of a service |
| [`annotation update`](#mcrl-annotation-update) | Replace a graph annotation |

## mcrl annotation create

Create a graph annotation.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl annotation create --service <service> --title <title> [flags]

Aliases:
  create, new

Create a graph annotation. --from defaults to now and --to to --from.

API: POST /api/v0/graph-annotations
API key permission: Read, Write

Examples:
  mcrl annotation create --service web --title "deploy v1.2.3"
  mcrl annotation create --service web --role app --title "load test" --from 13:00 --to 14:30

Flags:
      --description string   description (up to 1024 characters)
  -f, --file string          JSON or YAML file in the API's format ("-" for stdin); flags override its fields
      --from string          start time (default "now")
      --role stringArray     attach to this role of the service instead of the whole service (repeatable)
      --service string       service name
      --title string         title (up to 250 characters)
      --to string            end time (default: same as --from)
```

## mcrl annotation delete

Delete a graph annotation.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl annotation delete <annotation-id>

Aliases:
  delete, rm

Delete a graph annotation.

API: DELETE /api/v0/graph-annotations/<id>
API key permission: Read, Write

Examples:
  mcrl annotation delete 3Ja1bAxcdef
  mcrl annotation list --service web --jq '.[] | select(.title | startswith("test")) | .id' | xargs -n1 mcrl annotation delete --yes
```

## mcrl annotation list

List graph annotations of a service.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl annotation list --service <service> [flags]

Aliases:
  list, ls

List graph annotations of a service that overlap the time range
(default: the last 7 days).

API: GET /api/v0/graph-annotations
API key permission: Read

Examples:
  mcrl annotation list --service web
  mcrl annotation list --service web --since 30d --jq '.[].title'

Flags:
      --service string   service name (required)
      --since string     start of the time range (default "7d")
      --until string     end of the time range (default "now")
```

## mcrl annotation update

Replace a graph annotation.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl annotation update <annotation-id> --service <service> --title <title> [flags]

Replace a graph annotation. The API has no way to fetch one annotation,
so give every field again (flags or -f), as for create.

API: PUT /api/v0/graph-annotations/<id>
API key permission: Read, Write

Examples:
  mcrl annotation update 3Ja1bAxcdef --service web --title "deploy v1.2.3 (rolled back)" --from 13:00 --to 13:20

Flags:
      --description string   description (up to 1024 characters)
  -f, --file string          JSON or YAML file in the API's format ("-" for stdin); flags override its fields
      --from string          start time (default "now")
      --role stringArray     attach to this role of the service instead of the whole service (repeatable)
      --service string       service name
      --title string         title (up to 250 characters)
      --to string            end time (default: same as --from)
```

## mcrl annotation wrap

Run a command and record it as a graph annotation.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl annotation wrap --service <service> --title <title> -- <command> [args...] [flags]

Run a command and record its run time as a graph annotation.

The annotation is created when the command starts and updated with the end
time when it finishes. If the command fails, " (failed: exit N)" is added
to the title. The command's output is passed through, a note about the
annotation goes to stderr, and mcrl exits with the command's exit code.

API: POST /api/v0/graph-annotations, PUT /api/v0/graph-annotations/<id>
API key permission: Read, Write

Examples:
  mcrl annotation wrap --service web --title "deploy $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)" -- ./deploy.sh
  mcrl annotation wrap --service db --role primary --title "VACUUM" -- psql -c 'VACUUM ANALYZE'

Flags:
      --description string   description (up to 1024 characters)
  -f, --file string          JSON or YAML file in the API's format ("-" for stdin); flags override its fields
      --from string          start time (default "now")
      --role stringArray     attach to this role of the service instead of the whole service (repeatable)
      --service string       service name
      --title string         title (up to 250 characters)
      --to string            end time (default: same as --from)
```
